title: Fats Waller hears him at Small's and sends for him
summary: Fats saw him in the club; drummer Arnold Bolling and Bud Scripp woke him at home to ask him to record with Fats at Victor.

story.theme_name: In the studio: making records, then and now
story.community_name: My first record date: sessions, personnel, discography

blocks.x: Fats is in the club one night, and he saw me doing this. So he asked somebody, who is that guy?
After he heard me play. Say his name is Herman Autrey. Herman Autrey? Yeah. But -- Bud Scrippy, Arnold Bolding, did you ever hear of him?

Very fine drummer. He was with -- Arnold played some with everybody. Wait a minute, some of the big bands, a lot of the big bands. Wait a minute. Dog-gone it, I don't know where I am. (Snaps fingers.) Some of the bigger -- Don Redman Bradman. He played with -- what the heck, Arnold played with some of the best bands around town.

Anyway, I'm -- see I'm -- I mean said where does he live? So I said I live down the street, 123rd -- 129th Street, at the end of Seventh Avenue. So he told -- I asked him if he'd like to do some records with me. Fats. I'm laying up in bed asleep with my wife, Herman! I said what? Herman! He says, hey, he says, 'how you doing? My name is Arnold, this is Bud Scripp, you know me.' I say yes, Scripp, you with Arnold Bolling.
He says Fats Waller sent me down and ask you if -- would you like to do some records with him. I say man, (Pants), like I was speechless. I said certainly, sure. He

says okay. That's it. He went back and told him. So he says well go to this address, and he says (unintelligible). I say my name is Herman Autrey. He says well I'm Fats, hello, come on in, and he made (unintelligible). We met each other. What did you think? I said man, I'd be tickled to death, you know. You know the rest of the story from there.
No, I want to hear the rest of the story from there.

Well I mean -- would you like to make some? I say yes sir! I'd be very happy, tickled to death. And I never made a record in my life, and never been near a studio, and I'm -- you know, so I'm all everything, elated, and everything.
So he said okay. Meet me down at Victor's studios tomorrow morning at 8:00 o'clock, at 24th Street, and --
I -- yeah. I guess. It's been so long. I would be there. So man! You should have seen me getting down, and standing in front of the doorway, for this place to open, and --
